name: bds_persistence_extras
description: Read and Write beyond test 14; records built with an independent Python packer. BDS A (IDs from 599: BDS 599, developers 0x1010 = 600, 0x3110 = 601, map 602, node 603) only provides developer objects. BDS B (604) reads a crafted 177-byte record: null map and node; developers {0x1010: 600, 0x3110: null (skipped), 0x4300: 999 (unknown to the host: skipped, [choice])}; special buildings [70, null (skipped), 71] appended with a reference each; stages {0x1010: 3, 0x4300: 7}; marks 0x1010 {(2, 1), (-1, 5), (2, -3)} and an empty 0x3110 entry, merged into the process-wide set; planned growth {600, (4, 5), stage 2, day 1234} inserted and its developer reference released, and one for developer 999 skipped; cheats (1, 0, 1). Read true, all 177 bytes consumed, loadedFromSave. Init then calls Init again on 600 (no creation), creates 0x3110 (605), keeps the loaded stages (no reset to 0), creates the map (606) and node (607, supply 100) because the record had none, and sets lastSuccessfulBuild to today for both developers. Writing B gives 152 bytes: map 606, node 607, developers ascending, specials in list order, stages ascending, marks ascending by type with cells ascending by signed (x, z): (-1, 5), (2, -3), (2, 1); the empty set is written with 0 cells; the planned growth entry; cheats 01 00 01. References: developer 600 is held by A and B (2), 605 by B (1); specials 70 and 71 one each. Replacement: BDS C (608; developers 609 and 610) reads {0x1010: 601}: its old 0x1010 developer 609 is released (0 references) and the map holds 601 (2 references: A's and C's); reading the same developer again keeps one map reference ([choice]). A truncated record (22 bytes, inside the first developer reference) -> Read false; what was read before the end is kept (loadedFromSave true).
